Bolton Bailey said:

Christos might also be interested in the ProbComp type from VCVio.

@Bolton Bailey :
I took a look at this and current it seems to be an oracle whose model assumes uniform distribution on a type. As you know I have a similar model for algorithms and complexity, and in particular probabilistic computation. But I encounter two kinds of scenarios:

  1. In one case, I need distribution agnostic queries which have to get results for any distribution (think PAC learning models.
  2. In a different case, I need distribution specific queries where the queries are only analysed under pre-specified distributions (like uniform or gaussian).

Have you experimented with queries which explicitly specify distributions? If yes, Have you run into any issues with doing so?
Can't say I have - I mostly have used VCVio just in implementing cryptographic primitives that happen to assume distributions are uniform.

There was actually a problem I was interested in at one point: Say we want to implement an oracle that accepts some polygon (with rational vertices, say) and returns the count of points from a poisson process that fall in that polygon, and which remains consistent across queries. I was interested in what data structures we could use to write such an oracle and the time complexity for a query.

But I remember thinking it would even be hard to define an oracle that I could compute with even to sample something like a Poisson(1) random variable, because the PMF of that variable has irrational values, and I think ProbComp is only capable of computing distributions with rational PMFs. So I'm not sure what it would look like do be able to return a variable where there are irrational probabilities. If I pseudorandomly generate some values and then pretend they are uniformly random, I will still have sampled a finite amount of data, and so there will be a finite number of outcomes, and I will have rational probabilities for all of my outcomes.

Thanks for the discussion and comments on VCVio! We are aware that the default path for oracle computations in the library assume a uniform distribution semantic (hence response type needs to be nonempty and finite); however there is ongoing work to remove that restriction: https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/VCV-io/pull/402

Much of the machinery of VCVio remains distribution agnostic
